title: 6.6.21 Fix the Broken Pseudocode: the Pause State
description: Repair half-finished pseudocode for a pause feature: give the not-playing frame its own branch, wire in the pause screen, stop a step jumping to itself, and add the way out.

steps.title: Repair the half-finished pseudocode
steps.instructions:
Here is what the finished feature should do, in plain English:

**1.** When the state is play: update the game, and if p was pressed, change the state to paused.

**2.** When the state is not play (it is paused): draw the pause screen, and if p was pressed, change the state back to play.

**3.** Every path ends at the end of the frame. No step may send you back to itself.

The same plan is drawn as a flow chart above the editor. You do not draw it, you read it: follow the arrows and match each box to one of the steps.

Someone started this pseudocode and stopped halfway. It is already in `README.md`. **Press Run before changing anything**: four checks should be red. Read each red card against the plan above, then repair it. Do not start over. The call names are `updateGame` and `drawPauseScreen`. A new keyword for this repair: `ELSE` starts the branch for every other case. In a different program: `IF door is open` ... `ELSE` ... `END IF`. The ELSE belongs to the decision it lines up with, so close the inner decision first.

Renumber the lines if you like: every line just needs a number.

When it is all green, check the thing no check covers: can the player get out of pause? Green means legal, not finished.
hints: A step that jumps back to itself is a hung game, written down.
Think about which frames the pause screen should run on.

requirements.title: Every frame that is not playing is handled
requirements.description: The play decision has a branch for the frames when the game is not playing.
requirements.hint: Frames that are not playing need their own branch. Check where it sits: it should line up with the play decision, after the inner END IF.

requirements.title: The pause screen is drawn only when paused
requirements.description: The call to drawPauseScreen runs only on the paused frames.
requirements.hint: The pause screen should be drawn only on paused frames. Where does that put the call?

requirements.title: Every step moves forward
requirements.description: No step sends you back to an earlier step. A state change is an ordinary step.
requirements.hint: Look for a step that sends the flow back to itself: that is a hung game, written down.

requirements.title: The player can leave pause
requirements.description: The paused branch checks for p and goes back to play.
requirements.hint: A paused game needs a way back to playing. What should the paused frames check for?

requirements.title: Pausing needs a key press
requirements.description: The change to paused sits inside the check for p.
requirements.hint: Think about what has to happen before the state can change to paused.

requirements.title: Playing updates the game
requirements.description: The play branch updates the game, and the paused frames do not.
requirements.hint: The play branch (before the ELSE) should CALL updateGame. A paused game must not update.

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A([draw runs]) --> B{is the game playing?}
  B -- yes --> C[[update the game]]
  C --> D{p pressed?}
  D -- yes --> E[switch to paused]
  D -- no --> Z([end of frame])
  E --> Z
  B -- no --> F[[draw the pause screen]]
  F --> G{p pressed?}
  G -- yes --> H[switch to play]
  G -- no --> Z
  H --> Z
planChart.caption: The finished pause feature. The not-playing branch draws the pause screen and has a way back to play.
